title: SpaceX Launches 27 Starlink Satellites From California After Three Scrubs
excerpt: Starlink 15-15 lifted off from Vandenberg on its fourth attempt as booster B1063 flew a 36th time, while Florida's Falcon 9 cadence pauses for Starship.
body:
• SpaceX launched the Starlink 15-15 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Friday, October 23, lifting off at 3:48 p.m. PDT with 27 Starlink satellites aboard a Falcon 9.
  • The launch succeeded on the fourth attempt after three days of scrubs caused by a technical issue and poor weather.
  • First-stage booster B1063 flew for the 36th time and landed on a droneship about eight and a half minutes after liftoff, becoming only the second Falcon 9 booster to reach three dozen flights.
  • For readers who rely on Starlink at home or for remote work: SpaceX says it added 1.6 million customers in the third quarter and now serves 174 markets, and each California launch adds capacity to the network.

SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites from California on Friday afternoon, ending a stop-start week at Vandenberg Space Force Base and adding another batch to a constellation the company says now numbers more than 11,100 satellites in low Earth orbit.

The Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at 3:48 p.m. PDT (6:48 p.m. EDT / 2248 UTC) on October 23, flying a southeasterly trajectory from the pad, according to Spaceflight Now, which covered the mission live. The flight, designated Starlink 15-15, was recorded as a launch success by Next Spaceflight, listing 27 payloads on a Falcon 9 Block 5.

Fourth attempt after three scrubs

The launch came after three consecutive days of aborted attempts. An attempt on Tuesday was called off because of a technical issue, bad weather stopped the countdown before fueling on Wednesday, and on Thursday the launch director called a hold in the final seconds of the countdown because of poor weather, Spaceflight Now reported. Friday's attempt lifted off without a further hold.

https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2113786051009696177

The mission used first-stage booster B1063, flying for the 36th time. Spaceflight Now said it will become the second Falcon 9 booster to reach three dozen flights. Roughly eight and a half minutes after liftoff, B1063 landed on a droneship at sea, which Spaceflight Now counted as the 673rd Falcon booster landing to date.

The booster previously supported missions including Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich, NASA's DART, Transporter-7 and several national-security payloads, alongside 26 earlier Starlink flights.

Starlink growth behind the launch cadence

The California launch came days after SpaceX reported its third-quarter results. Speaking on the earnings call on Tuesday, October 20, hours before the first Starlink 15-15 attempt, SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell said the company added 1.6 million Starlink customers in the three-month period and that the service was active across 174 markets globally.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=hANSUkrKDwQ

"This number does not include additional hundreds of thousands of enterprise subscribers and aviation customers. We remain incredibly inspired by the impact of Starlink on communities around the world, including providing service to hundreds of thousands of students and teachers in schools globally, as well as for emergency response during natural disasters."

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, SpaceX said it closed the third quarter with more than 11,100 Starlink satellites in low Earth orbit, including the 26 Starlink Version 3 satellites launched during Starship Flight 14. The filing put connectivity revenue for the quarter at $5.2 billion, up 22 percent from the previous quarter.

Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen told the call that the satellite roadmap is a key driver of future connectivity growth. Through the end of the year and throughout 2027, SpaceX expects to deploy Starlink V3 satellites in meaningful volume on Starship, with each Starship launch ramping toward a payload delivering more than 20 times the downlink capacity of a current Falcon 9 launch, he said.

Florida cadence slows as Starship takes priority

While Vandenberg keeps flying Starlink missions, Falcon 9 activity in Florida is entering a deliberate pause. SpaceX Vice President of Launch Kiko Dontchev said this week there will be a six-week gap between Falcon 9 launches from the Cape while crews prepare for Starship, according to Florida Today. The Space Coast's most recent Falcon 9 lifted off on Tuesday, October 20, on the Bandwagon-5 mission.

https://www.instagram.com/p/De20xocoHm_/

"If you haven't seen a signal that it's 'game time' on Starship, that's it."

Florida Today reported that SpaceX's Starlink missions have moved westward to Vandenberg, and that the Cape's launch cadence has markedly dwindled since August 25, when Starlink 10-49 marked the final time a Falcon 9 carried Starlink satellites from Florida. Dontchev said Starship launch infrastructure at Kennedy Space Center's pad 39A is effectively complete, and SpaceX still hopes to launch the first Starship from Florida by the end of the year.

For now, Falcon 9 remains the vehicle building out Starlink from California, one 27-satellite batch at a time, while the larger Starship system that is meant to take over the heaviest deployment work prepares for its next flight in November.
